column2: What can I ask “Ask a question”?
column3: Search → Ask a question in French, or straight in the quick search (⌘K): a question is recognised on its own, “🔎 Ask the question” shows at the top, then the short answer (“Petrus MAZAUD : 2 enfants”). Questions are written in French. You can ask: a person’s relatives (children, grandchildren, brothers and sisters, uncles and aunts, nephews and nieces, cousins, parents-in-law, sons-in-law, godparents…); “mes grands-parents”, “ma grand-mère paternelle”, “mes cousins germains”, “mon lien avec Paul Mazaud” (“me” = the starting person); “qui est Jean Dupont ?” (summary and link to the record); lists with a place, an occupation, dates (“vers 1850”, “années 1850”, “au XIXe siècle”), an OR (“nés à Lille ou à Quimper”, “laboureurs ou tisserands”) or something missing (“sans date de décès”, “qui ne sont pas nées à Lille”, “sans parents connus”, “sans source”); “mort à la guerre”, “les vivants”; calculations (records, averages, most frequent first names). Common mistakes are understood (“enfans”, “Petrus Mazeau”, “à lille”, “St Pierre”) and shown in “I understood”. A word that was not read is flagged: “I did not take into account: …”. For missing records, “where to look”, duplicates or ⚖️ estate files (heirs, overdue deadlines, letters without a reply), the answer sends you to the tool with a button. Settings → 🔎 Search: “Answer questions in the quick search” (yes or no).
